body_markdown:
With Cleva’s US remittance product recently launched, the Cleva vs Wise question is a question that’ll definitely come up where Nigerians in the United States trade tips on the cheapest, fastest way to send money home. Both platforms offer transparent pricing and let you move dollars to naira within minutes.


But for Nigerian families relying on support from abroad, Cleva offers more than Wise beyond simple money transfers. This guide breaks down fees, exchange rates, speed, and the extra features that matter most to the diaspora, so you can decide with confidence.


## **Wise: A Quick Overview**


Before getting into the full Cleva vs Wise breakdown, it helps to know what each platform actually is. Wise stands out for its mid-market exchange rates, transparent fees, and reliable international money transfers.


Sending $1,000 to Nigeria the cheapest way, using funds already sitting in a Wise balance, costs $5.78, and the platform shows the fee before you confirm anything ([Wise](https://wise.com/us/send-money/send-money-to-nigeria) ). Funding a transfer with a debit card through direct debit instead adds a fee of roughly $1.17 plus 0.8% of the amount sent ([RemitAnalyst](https://remitanalyst.com/send-money-to-nigeria-from-usa/remit-profiles/transferwise/) ).


Delivery speed depends heavily on how you fund the transfer. Some payments arrive within seconds, while direct debit transfers can take four to five business days.


Wise is not built specifically for Nigerians. It supports over 40 currencies and serves millions of customers worldwide. That broad approach means it doesn’t specifically cater to how Nigerians in the diaspora spend. Nigerians may need to pay a parent’s electricity bill, top up a sibling’s data, or save for family goals back home.


## **Cleva: A Quick Overview**


Understanding Cleva’s design philosophy is the second half of the Cleva vs Wise picture. Cleva built its product specifically for Nigerians and Africans in the diaspora. You can see that focus across almost every part of the Cleva vs Wise comparison. With Cleva, U.S. users get a real USD account with a routing and account number. They can fund transfers instantly with a debit card and send naira to any Nigerian bank account in minutes, with no conversion markup.


Beyond moving money, Cleva lets you pay a loved one’s electricity bill or buy them mobile data directly from the U.S., something Wise simply does not offer. You also earn Cleva Points on every transfer and can redeem them for real USD. With Cleva Pots, you can set money aside and earn up to 3% in rewards.


This difference sits at the heart of the Cleva vs Wise comparison. Wise focuses on moving money, while Cleva helps Nigerians in the diaspora manage and use their money for the things that matter to their families back home.


## **Cleva vs Wise: Fees and exchange rates**


Fees are usually the first thing people compare, and it is where the Cleva vs Wise conversation gets interesting. Wise is transparent about its costs, but transparency does not always mean cheap: card-funded transfers carry a percentage-based fee on top of a flat charge, and that cost scales up as the amount you send grows.


Cleva takes a different approach for the diaspora use case. You can fund transfers with a debit card without paying a conversion markup. Cleva sends naira from your USD account to Nigerian banks without the layered fees of Wise’s card-funding route.


On top of that, Cleva rewards every transfer with Cleva Points redeemable for real dollars, effectively giving money back on transactions where Wise gives nothing back at all.


The table below lays the Cleva vs Wise numbers side by side.


**Feature** **Cleva** **Wise**


**Built for the Nigerian diaspora** Yes No, general-purpose


**Conversion markup** None Mid-market rate plus service fee


**Funding by debit card** Instant, no conversion fee Fee plus 0.8% of amount


**Transfer speed to Nigerian bank** Minutes Seconds to 5 business days, depending on funding method


**Pay electricity bills in Nigeria from the U.S.** Yes, 1% discount Not available


**Buy data for family in Nigeria from the U.S.** Yes, 3% discount Not available


**Rewards on transfers** Cleva Points, redeemable for USD None


**Savings feature with rewards** Pots, 3% rewards None


## **Cleva vs Wise: Speed and Reliability**


Wise advertises that a majority of its transfers arrive in under 20 seconds, but that figure applies mainly to balance-funded transfers and does not reflect every route. Direct debit transfers, which many first-time U.S. users default to, can take four to five business days to clear before the recipient in Nigeria sees the naira.


Cleva takes a different approach with its core U.S.-to-Nigeria route. You can fund your transfer with a debit card, and Cleva credits the recipient’s Nigerian bank account within minutes, not days. For a family waiting on money for rent, school fees, or an emergency, that reliability is the difference between a stressful wait and instant peace of mind, and it’s another point in Cleva’s favor in the Cleva vs Wise comparison.


## **Cleva vs Wise: Bill payments that actually help family back home**


This is where the Cleva vs Wise comparison stops being close. Sending cash is useful, but it does not always solve the actual problem a family in Nigeria is facing. Cleva lets you pay for data or settle an electricity bill directly from the U.S., in real time, at a discount: 3% off data purchases and 1% off electricity payments.


Instead of wiring naira and hoping it gets used the right way, you can settle the exact bill yourself, straight from your phone in the U.S. Wise has no equivalent feature. It focuses on money transfers and multi-currency accounts. Recipients in Nigeria still need to handle bill payments separately and manually.


## **Cleva vs Wise: Rewards and long-term savings**


Every transfer on Cleva earns Cleva Points, which are redeemable for real USD, turning routine sending into an activity that pays you back over time. Cleva also offers Pots, a savings feature that lets users set money aside and earn 3% in rewards while it sits there, something particularly useful for diaspora families saving toward school fees, a wedding, or a home project back in Nigeria.


Wise has no comparable loyalty or savings-reward system; its value proposition begins and ends with the transfer itself. When you add up the rewards, the discounts on bills, and the savings features, the Cleva vs Wise comparison shows that Cleva is doing more with every dollar sent.


## **Cleva vs Wise: Which one should you choose?**


Weighing up every factor in the Cleva vs Wise comparison makes the answer fairly clear for most Nigerian families abroad. If all you need is a one-off, generic international transfer to a country that isn’t Nigeria, Wise remains a reliable, well-established option.


For Nigerians in the U.S. who send money home regularly, the Cleva vs Wise comparison tilts firmly toward Cleva. You get faster delivery on the core route, no conversion markup, and real rewards through Cleva Points. You can also save with Cleva Pots, earn up to 3% in rewards, and pay electricity and data bills directly for loved ones at a discount.


Wise was not built with these needs in mind; Cleva was.


## **Conclusion**


The Cleva vs Wise comparison ultimately comes down to who each platform was built for. Wise is a solid, transparent global money-transfer tool, but it was designed for a broad international audience, not specifically for the day-to-day realities of supporting family in Nigeria. Cleva was.


From free debit-card funding and fast delivery to discounted electricity and data payments, Cleva Points rewards, and a Pots savings feature that earns 3%, Cleva gives you more ways to help your loved ones and more value back for doing it.
